MUJAHID:v1p374#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p374#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p374#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says the sun passes them on their left and leaves them there.

MUJAHID:v1p374#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p374#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p374#2/r2.claim: Mujahid says the youths' cave lay between two mountains.

MUQATIL:18:13-17/r11.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:13-17/r11.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:13-17/r11.claim: At sunrise the sun inclines away from the cave to the right and leaves the youths; at sunset it passes them on the left.

MUQATIL:18:13-17/r12.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:13-17/r12.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:13-17/r12.claim: Qaraḍah means it leaves them, and fajwah means a corner or open space in the cave.

MUQATIL:18:13-17/r13.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:13-17/r13.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:13-17/r13.claim: This arrangement is among God's signs and workmanship; whoever He guides to Islam is guided, while the misguided has no guiding companion.

MUQATIL:18:13-17/r14.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:13-17/r14.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:13-17/r14.claim: A wali is a companion, and a murshid is one who guides to guidance; the misguided person's ally shares his error.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p174#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p174#2/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p174#2/r2.claim: The sun veers away from the cave at sunrise and leaves the sleepers to the side at sunset; al-Hasan says sunlight never enters the cave.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p174#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p174#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p174#2/r3.claim: Qatāda says the sleepers lie in a broad open space inside the cave; this arrangement is a sign.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p174#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p174#2/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p174#2/r4.claim: God guides whoever He wills, while no protective guide can be found for someone He leaves astray.

FARRA:v2p136#2/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p136#2/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p136#2/r2.claim: تزاور may be read with assimilation of the first ت into ز; other readings are تزور and تزوار, like تحمر and تحمار.

FARRA:v2p136#2/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p136#2/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p136#2/r3.claim: The sun's azwarar means it rose to the cave's right without entering, then passed by their left at sunset; قرضته and حذوته mean it was alongside them.

FARRA:v2p137/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p137/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p137/r1.claim: فجوة means a spacious open area or side.

MAJAZ:v1p394/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p394/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p394/r4.claim: Tazāwar means lean or turn aside, from zawr, crookedness or inclination; Ibn Muqbil's verse witnesses zūr.

MAJAZ:v1p394/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p394/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p394/r5.claim: Abū al-Zaḥḥāf al-Kulābī's poem uses azwar for an inclined place.

MAJAZ:v1p394/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p394/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p394/r6.claim: Taqriḍuhum means the sun leaves them on its left, passes alongside, or cuts past them.

MAJAZ:v1p394/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p394/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p394/r7.claim: Dhū al-Rummah's verse shows objects passing to the left and riders to the right.

MAJAZ:v1p396/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p396/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p396/r1.claim: Fajwah means an open space; its plural forms include fajawāt and fijāʾ.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p400/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p400/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p400/r1.claim: Qatada says the sun veered away from their cave on the right.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p400/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p400/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p400/r2.claim: He explains the sun's passing them on the left as leaving them to that side.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264#4/r1.claim: Tazāwar means the sun slants away.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264#4/r2.claim: Taqriḍuhum means the sun turns away and passes beyond them on the left, as in Dhū al-Rumma's verse.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264#4/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264#4/r3.speaker: ذو الرمة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264#4/r3.claim: Dhū al-Rumma uses yaqriḍna for camels passing a place, attesting the sense “pass beyond.”

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264#4/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264#4/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264#4/r4.claim: Fajwa means an open, spacious place, with plural forms fajawāt and fijaʾ; maqnaʾa is also said, but the first better matches Arabic usage.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264#4/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264#4/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264#4/r5.claim: Waṣīd is the threshold rather than the courtyard: awṣada means to close a door, bringing it against the threshold; this lets the dog be inside the cave.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264#4/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264#4/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264#4/r6.claim: Waṣīd may also mean the door itself; a poem uses it in that sense, with the dog lying at the entrance.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264#4/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264#4/r7.speaker: شاعر
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p264#4/r7.claim: An unnamed poet uses waṣīd for a doorway, attesting the alternate sense “door.”

TUSTARI:18:17/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:18:17/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:18:17/r1.claim: God’s leading someone astray means allowing the wretchedness already known of that person to appear by withholding protection; no one can then protect him.

TAB-FULL:v15p184/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p184/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p184/r1.claim: Tazawwar means that the rising sun turns or leans away from the cave, from the root for crookedness or turning aside.

TAB-FULL:v15p184/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p184/r2.speaker: بشر بن أبي خازم
TAB-FULL:v15p184/r2.claim: Bishr ibn Abi Khazim's verse uses izwirar to mean turning away or avoidance.

TAB-FULL:v15p184/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p184/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p184/r3.claim: Most Medinan, Meccan, and Basran readers double the zay, while most Kufans read it lightly; both forms are established and close in meaning.

TAB-FULL:v15p184/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p184/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p184/r4.claim: Some also transmit tazur with a light initial t and geminated r, and tazwar in the pattern of tahmar.

TAB-FULL:v15p184/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p184/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p184/r5.claim: Both well-known readings, with light or doubled zay, are correct; the two rarer variants are linguistically possible but too anomalous to read.

TAB-FULL:v15p184/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p184/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v15p184/r6.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr glosses tazawwar as turning or leaning.

TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r1.claim: At sunset the sun leaves the youths on the left; by passing away from both sides it avoids striking them, which otherwise could burn or bleach them.

TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r2.claim: Basran Arab usage takes qarada as cutting past and leaving something behind; the Kufans instead explain it as being opposite or alongside.

TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r3.claim: The root qarada means cutting, as in cutting cloth, scissors, or a mouse gnawing fabric.

TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r4.speaker: ذو الرمة
TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r4.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's line uses yaqriḍna to mean that the camels cut across or pass through the route.

TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the sunset clause as leaving the youths untouched.

TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r6.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the sun leaves them on the left at sunset.

TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r7.claim: Mujahid glosses taqriḍuhum as leaving them.

TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p186#2/r8.claim: Qatada also explains the sunset clause as leaving the youths alone on the left.

TAB-FULL:v15p186/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p186/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p186/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the sun leans away from the youths on the right at sunrise and on both sides as it passes.

TAB-FULL:v15p186/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p186/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p186/r2.claim: Qatada explains that the sun inclines rightward and leaves the youths untouched on that side.

TAB-FULL:v15p186/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p186/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p186/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says direct exposure would have burned them, and without being turned from side to side the earth would have consumed them.

TAB-FULL:v15p188/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p188/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p188/r1.claim: Qatada says the setting sun leaves the youths on the left; Sa'id ibn Jubayr gives the same gloss, leaving them.

TAB-FULL:v15p189/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p189/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p189/r1.claim: Fajwa means an open, spacious area within the cave; its plural forms are fajawat and the extended fajāʾ.

TAB-FULL:v15p189/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p189/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p189/r2.claim: Qatada glosses the cave's fajwa as an open space.

TAB-FULL:v15p189/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p189/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v15p189/r3.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr explains fajwa as the inner place of the cave.

TAB-FULL:v15p189/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p189/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p189/r4.claim: Mujahid glosses it as a remote or far-off place.

TAB-FULL:v15p190#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p190#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p190#2/r1.claim: Guidance and misguidance are in Gods hands; whoever is misled will find no ally to guide him to the truth.

TAB-FULL:v15p190#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p190#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p190#2/r2.claim: Muhammad should not grieve over his people's rejection, since guidance and misguidance belong to God, who could have guided them if He willed.

ZAJJAJ:v3p273#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p273#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p273#2/r1.claim: Fajwa means a spacious open area.

ZAJJAJ:v3p273#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p273#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p273#2/r2.claim: The claim that the cave faced the Pleiades and so received no sunlight is unclear; God made the sun avoid them at sunrise and sunset.

ZAJJAJ:v3p273#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p273#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p273#2/r3.claim: Most language has المهتدي with yāʾ; the codex omits it here, unlike al-Aʿraf, and noun yāʾ deletion is permitted while verbal deletion would mark jussive mood.

ZAJJAJ:v3p273/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p273/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p273/r1.claim: Tazāwar has several readings, including forms without alif; its origin is تتزاور with tāʾ assimilated into zāy.

ZAJJAJ:v3p273/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p273/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p273/r2.claim: For تقرضهم, the kasra reading is established and means the sun turns away from them and leaves them.

ZAJJAJ:v3p273/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p273/r3.speaker: ذو الرمة
ZAJJAJ:v3p273/r3.claim: Dhu al-Rumma uses يقرضن for leaving or turning away, witnessing this sense of تقرضهم.

ZAJJAJ:v3p273/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p273/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p273/r4.claim: The root qarḍ means cutting and separating, as in asking someone to cut off a dirham.

NAHHAS:v2p450/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p450/r10.speaker: أهل الكوفة
NAHHAS:v2p450/r10.claim: They read tazāwar with the first tāʾ deleted.

NAHHAS:v2p450/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p450/r11.speaker: قتادة وابن أبي إسحاق وابن عامر
NAHHAS:v2p450/r11.claim: They read tazawwar, on the pattern of taḥammar.

NAHHAS:v2p450/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p450/r12.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v2p450/r12.claim: He also records tazwār, patterned like taḥmār.

NAHHAS:v2p450/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p450/r9.speaker: أهل الحرمين وأبو عمرو
NAHHAS:v2p450/r9.claim: They assimilate the tāʾ into zāy in tazāwar; its unassimilated form is tatazāwar.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p131/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p131/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p131/r1.claim: They read تزاور with a doubled zāy; Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisai lighten it, while Ibn Amir reads تزور.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p131/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p131/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p131/r2.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses تزاور عن كهفهم as inclining away from their cave, from the sense of ميل and انحراف.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p131/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p131/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p131/r3.claim: The doubled form can result from deleting the second tāʾ, as deletion lightens a form much like assimilation; its sense is the sun's turning away to the right.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p131/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p131/r4.speaker: أبو الحسن
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p131/r4.claim: Abu al-Hasan says Ibn Amir's تزور does not normally mean the sun's inclination, but al-Farisi defends that sense with poetry using ازورار for turning away.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r2.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p148/r2.claim: Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr retain yāʾ in connection for their listed forms, add المهتدي, and omit it at pauses because these endings resemble rhyme.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p25/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p25/r1.speaker: الجحدري
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p25/r1.claim: Al-Jaḥdarī reads تزوار in the ifʿāl pattern; the author notes that this pattern usually describes colors or visible defects but has other attestations.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p25/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p25/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p25/r2.claim: Because ifʿāl is intransitive, the object خليلًا in the cited poem depends on an implied verb such as serve, care for, or replace.

SULAMI:v1p404#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p404#5/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p404#5/r1.claim: Their added guidance was light upon light and proof upon proof; the sun shifted from their cave because their stronger light threatened to eclipse it.

SULAMI:v1p404#5/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p404#5/r2.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p404#5/r2.claim: The person's right side is the heart and the left is the self; divine care alternates between them, or the person would perish.

SULAMI:v1p404#5/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p404#5/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p404#5/r3.claim: God adorned them with contentment; the sun submitted to their lights and fled from the cave's light.

SULAMI:v1p404#5/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p404#5/r4.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p404#5/r4.claim: Only someone trying to reach God through personal effort is veiled from Him; arrival comes by seeking through His divine attribute.

SULAMI:v1p405/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p405/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p405/r1.claim: The guided person receives faith's beginning and end without personal cause, through divine qualities rather than human ones, and is characterized by God's attributes rather than his own.

SULAMI:v1p405/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p405/r2.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p405/r2.claim: No one can avert a person's wretched fate once God has decreed it.

THALABI:v6p160/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p160/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p160/r1.claim: The sun's course and cave conditions are among God's wonders and proofs of His power and wisdom.

THALABI:v6p160/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p160/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p160/r2.claim: Guidance and misguidance belong to God; whoever God guides is guided, and the misled person has no directing guardian.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r1.claim: تزاور may mean that the sunlight turns away from the cave and does not touch it.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r10.claim: Another interpretation takes فجوة as a desolate place.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r11.speaker: الأخفش
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r11.claim: فجوة may mean a broad, open side of the cave; a poem uses it for an open valley or expanse.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r2.claim: Alternatively, it means that the sun inclines away from the cave to the right.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r3.speaker: الكسائي والفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r3.claim: تقرضهم may mean that the sun faces or passes alongside them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r4.claim: Alternatively, it means the sun cuts past them while deviating from them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r5.claim: A third view says the sun lends them a little of its rays and then withdraws them; they may have had no roof, and direct sunlight could have burned them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r6.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r6.claim: The cave may have faced the Big Dipper, which kept sunlight from reaching it at sunrise and sunset.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r7.claim: Alternatively, God diverted the sun to preserve their bodies and make them a sign to observers or those who heard of them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r8.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r8.claim: فجوة means an open space within the cave.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p290/r9.claim: فجوة may mean the inside of the cave.

QUSHAYRI:v2p211/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p211/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p211/r6.claim: Outwardly, sunlight did not spread over the youths in their part of the cave, even as winds blew over them.

QUSHAYRI:v2p211/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p211/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p211/r7.claim: The youths' lights of gnosis surpass sunlight: the sun illuminates creatures outwardly, while their knowledge illuminates the Real inwardly.

QUSHAYRI:v2p211/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p211/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p211/r8.claim: The sun's rays turning away indicates an event contrary to ordinary nature and may be counted among the saints' marvels.

QUSHAYRI:v2p212/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p212/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p212/r1.claim: God guides some through proofs and others through unveiled certainty: the first know by inference, while the latter experience communion as if by direct sight.

QUSHAYRI:v2p212/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p212/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p212/r2.claim: Those branded with deprivation have no gnosis, knowledge, or faith.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p550/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p550/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p550/r1.claim: The address to the viewer is hypothetical: it means that if you saw the sun at sunrise, you would see it turn away from their cave.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p550/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p550/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p550/r2.claim: He glosses tazāwar as moving away; in another report he says it tilts away from the youths.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p550/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p550/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p550/r3.claim: Tazāwar means to lean or turn, paralleling tamāyal; a poem describing a horse uses tamāyal as evidence.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p550/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p550/r4.speaker: أهل الكوفة وابن عامر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p550/r4.claim: The Kufans read the verb without the extra ta of the reciprocal form, while Ibn Amir reads tazawwar.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p550/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p550/r5.speaker: أبو الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p550/r5.claim: He objects that azwar is not used for leaning away, only for being withdrawn or contracted; Antara line about recoiling from a spear supports that sense.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p550/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p550/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p550/r6.claim: Jarir line about the palanquins turning away from a tree supports using the verb for the sun apparent turning aside.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r1.claim: Dhāt al-yamīn means toward the right; dhāt stands in for a directional noun, and al-Akhfash parses it as an adverb.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r10.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r10.claim: He rejects the explanation that their physical location alone blocked the sun; God withheld its approach, light, and heat by power as a sign.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r11.claim: The verse sign is God power to keep the sun from reaching them, rather than their lying in a naturally shaded place.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r2.speaker: الوالبي عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r2.claim: He glosses taqriḍuhum as leaving them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r3.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r3.claim: Qatada says the sun leaves them; Muqatil says it passes them by.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r4.speaker: الأخفش والزجاج وأبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r4.claim: They explain the sun as turning away from the youths and leaving them; al-Kisaʾi says the verb means to pass a place by.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r5.speaker: ذو الرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r5.claim: His line about riders passing mountain passes on their left illustrates taqriḍ as going past or bypassing.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r6.speaker: أبو عبيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r6.claim: He says qarḍ can mean cutting or traversing a land; a traveler who passed a place on the left has bypassed it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r7.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r7.claim: He describes a cave in Roman territory oriented toward Banat Naʿsh: the sun passes the cave right at sunrise and its left at sunset without striking it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r8.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r8.claim: They say the cave was in a sunny, open place facing Banat Naʿsh, yet the sun path spared the youths from heat, exposure, and worn clothing.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r9.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p552/r9.claim: He infers that the sun never, or almost never, reached them, preserving their bodies.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p555/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p555/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p555/r1.claim: They lay in a broad part of the cave where cool air and a breeze could reach them; faja means an open, spacious area.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p555/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p555/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p555/r2.claim: He gives the plural forms of faja as fajawat and faja, and cites a report about moving quickly when one finds an open space.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p555/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p555/r3.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p555/r3.claim: He glosses faja as a place extending broadly in width; Ibn Abbas calls it spaciousness.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p555/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p555/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p555/r4.claim: The sun turning and passing away from the cave are signs of God power and kindness to the youths.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p555/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p555/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p555/r5.claim: God guided the youths, and a person is guided only by God guidance; the example of misguidance is Daqyanus and his followers, who have no guiding patron.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:17-18/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:17-18/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:17-18/r1.claim: The sun angled away from the cave at sunrise and passed beyond it at sunset, never directly striking the youths, preserving their bodies while allowing cool air into the open space.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:17-18/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:17-18/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:17-18/r2.claim: The sun's course is a sign of God's power and care for the cave's occupants; God himself guided them, and without him they would not have been guided.

JISHUMI:v6p4371/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4371/r1.speaker: ابن عامر ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v6p4371/r1.claim: They read تزور with a still zāy and doubled rāʾ; ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read تزاور, and the remaining readers use the doubled form with alif; all mean to incline away.

JISHUMI:v6p4371/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4371/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v6p4371/r4.claim: They retain the yāʾ in المهتدي, while the others drop it for ease.

JISHUMI:v6p4371/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4371/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4371/r7.claim: Tazāwur means inclining or deviating from something, from zawr meaning crookedness; qarḍ means cutting, hence poetry, a loan, and repayment.

JISHUMI:v6p4371/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4371/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4371/r8.claim: Fajwa is an open, spacious place; its plural is فجوات, with فجاء also used.

JISHUMI:v6p4373/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r1.claim: The sun tilts away to the right of the cave at dawn and passes them on the left at sunset, so its rays do not fall on them, according to al-Aṣamm and Abū Muslim.

JISHUMI:v6p4373/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r10.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r10.claim: He says the sun normally reaches all the earth except places screened from it, and a barrier kept it from the youths; the author rejects this account as not distinctive to them.

JISHUMI:v6p4373/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r11.claim: The sign may mean their sleep, rest, and preservation as a reward for obedience; alternatively the whole story—including 309 years alive without food and preserved bodies and clothes—is evidence of God's power.

JISHUMI:v6p4373/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r12.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r12.claim: One account says all these events were a miracle God displayed through a prophet among them, their eldest.

JISHUMI:v6p4373/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r13.claim: The signs show God's power and wisdom, and that He suffices those who obey and rely on Him while punishing those who disobey.

JISHUMI:v6p4373/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r14.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r14.claim: The guided person is one whom God establishes toward reward and honor; the one misled from Paradise has no guiding ally.

JISHUMI:v6p4373/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r15.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r15.claim: He says the guided person accepts God's guidance, while the lost person accepts Satan's instead.

JISHUMI:v6p4373/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r2.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r2.claim: He interprets qarḍ as giving them a little sunlight, then taking it away as the sun sets, like a returned coin whose value is reduced.

JISHUMI:v6p4373/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r3.claim: He explains qarḍ as leaving them alone.

JISHUMI:v6p4373/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r4.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r4.claim: He explains it as passing beyond them.

JISHUMI:v6p4373/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r5.speaker: أبو عبيد
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r5.claim: He says qaradt the place means that one passed it.

JISHUMI:v6p4373/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r6.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r6.claim: He says the sun leaves them, sparing them its heat and harm.

JISHUMI:v6p4373/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r7.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r7.claim: He describes the cave as broad and set back so its occupants could receive moving air without heat or harm from the sun.

JISHUMI:v6p4373/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r8.claim: God showed them kindness and protection, choosing a resting place facing Banāt Naʿsh so sun and heat would not alter their skin or wear their clothes, while a breeze reached the spacious cave.

JISHUMI:v6p4373/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r9.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v6p4373/r9.claim: He says the cave entrance faced the pole, so the sun did not strike it from the east or west.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p157#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p157#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p157#2/r1.claim: The sunlight's course is among God's signs and proofs of His power; whoever God guides is guided, while the one He misguides has no guiding ally.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p157/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p157/r1.speaker: ابن عامر ويعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p157/r1.claim: They read tazūr with a still zāy and doubled rāʾ, on the pattern of taḥmar.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p157/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p157/r2.speaker: أهل الكوفة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p157/r2.claim: The Kufan readers use a light zāy with fatḥa and a following alif; all readings mean that the sun inclines away.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p157/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p157/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p157/r3.claim: Taqriḍuhum means the sun leaves them and turns aside; the root qaraḍ means cutting.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p157/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p157/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p157/r4.claim: Fajwa is an open, spacious part of the cave.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p157/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p157/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p157/r5.claim: He says the cave faced Banāt Naʿsh, so sunlight never fell on it; God chose a sheltered, spacious place with fresh air but no heat or distress.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p157/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p157/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p157/r6.claim: Some reject Ibn Qutayba's account that cave orientation kept out the sun, saying God diverted it by His power.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#3/r1.claim: Tazāwar means to incline away; it comes from tatazāwar, with the initial tāʾ assimilated into zāy or deleted, and other readings retain or reshape the form.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#3/r2.claim: The readings tazwar and tazwār also come from zawr, inclination; zawr can mean deviation from truth.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#3/r3.claim: Dhāta al-yamīn means the direction called the right side.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#3/r4.claim: Taqriḍuhum means cut away from or avoid them; a line by Dhū al-Rumma uses the verb for cutting across.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#3/r5.claim: They remain in shade throughout the day although the open space would expose them to sun; God shields them. Alternatively, the open area lets cool air reach them.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#3/r6.claim: Their sun-protected location is a special sign of divine honor; alternatively, their whole story is a sign, and the cave entrance faced north toward Banāt Naʿsh.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#3/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p661#3/r7.claim: The verse praises the youths for striving and surrendering to God: He guided and aided them to attain this rare honor and great sign; the abandoned person has no guide after God leaves him.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r1.claim: The narrative omits the transition: they took refuge in the cave, God caused them to sleep, and they remained so.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r10.claim: Another group of readers who use taqriḍuhum says the afternoon sun reached them, benefiting their bodies while cutting them off from the rest of its path.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r2.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r2.claim: These readers assimilate the initial tāʾ in tazāwar; other readings simplify or reshape the form, but all mean that the sun veers, turns, or inclines.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r3.speaker: الأخفش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash explains tazāwar as turning away; zawr means inclination, as in an eye that looks askance, and poetry uses azwar for a slanted side.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abi Rabi'a's verse uses azwar for a body's side turned away in fear.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r5.speaker: عنترة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r5.claim: Antara's line uses the verb izwarra for turning aside from a spear strike.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r6.speaker: بشر بن أبي حازم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r6.claim: Bishr ibn Abi Hazim's poem uses izwirar for a deviation in direction.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r7.claim: A report about the expedition of Mu'ta says the Prophet noticed Abdullah ibn Rawaha's bier slanting away from the biers of Ja'far and Zayd.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r8.claim: Most readers use the feminine verb taqriḍuhum; a minority uses yaqriḍuhum, with the cave as subject, cutting them off from sunlight.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p502#2/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says the sun did not reach the sleepers at all; taqriḍuhum means that it left them untouched.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p503/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p503/r1.speaker: ذي الرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p503/r1.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's verse uses qarada for cutting across a place, supporting the sun's described course.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p503/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p503/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p503/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj and others say the cave faced the Pleiades; its upper part was sheltered from rain, while al-Zajjaj also treats the sun's behavior itself as a divine sign independent of the entrance's direction.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p503/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p503/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p503/r3.claim: Right and left most naturally refer to the cave as if its entrance were a person's face; alternatively they can be measured relative to the sun's rays.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p503/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p503/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p503/r4.claim: Fajwa means an open space; Qatada says open area and Ibn Jubayr says an inner place, with Prophetic usage also applying it to a gap in a route.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p503/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p503/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p503/r5.claim: The phrase 'that is among God's signs' points to the entire arrangement; on al-Zajjaj's view it singles out the sun's unusual course, followed by praise of God.

TABRISI:18:17-18#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:17-18#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:17-18#2/r1.claim: Fajwa is an open space or courtyard; ayqāẓ is the plural of awake, ruqūd the plural of sleeping, and waṣīd is the entrance or closed door, with variant forms waṣīd/asīd and awṣada/aṣada.

TABRISI:18:17-18#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:17-18#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:17-18#2/r2.claim: The clauses about sunrise, sunset, and the youths in the cave all depend on ‘you see’; their being in a spacious place is a circumstantial clause.

TABRISI:18:17-18#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:17-18#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:17-18#2/r4.claim: The muṣḥaf writes al-muhtad here without yāʾ but writes it with yāʾ in al-Aʿrāf; deleting yāʾ is permitted in nouns but not verbs, where it marks jussive mood.

TABRISI:18:17-18#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:17-18#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:17-18#3/r1.claim: At sunrise the sun slants away to the right, and at sunset it passes to the left without entering the cave; Ibn ʿAbbās glosses taqriḍuhum as passing them at an angle.

TABRISI:18:17-18#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:17-18#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:18:17-18#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains taqriḍuhum as the sun passing them while turned away from them.

TABRISI:18:17-18#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:17-18#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:18:17-18#3/r3.claim: Qatāda says the youths were in a broad open area inside the cave; the recess let in air but could not be seen from the entrance.

TABRISI:18:17-18#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:17-18#3/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:17-18#3/r4.claim: God chose a spacious, north-facing place that let in breezes while protecting the youths from sun, heat, fading skin color, and worn clothing; the cave mouth faced the Pole Star.

TABRISI:18:17-18#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:17-18#3/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:17-18#3/r5.claim: God’s guidance made the youths rightly guided; the people of their community represent those left without a guiding protector.

TABRISI:18:17-18/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:17-18/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:17-18/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and Yaʿqūb read tazāwar with gemination; the Kūfans lighten it; the other readers geminate it. Al-Ḥijāzīs geminate lummilt, while the others lighten it; al-Jaḥdarī has tazwār and al-Ḥasan reads the turning as an active verb.

TABRISI:18:17-18/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:17-18/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:17-18/r10.claim: Other senses of qarḍ include a tooth’s gnawing, commercial partnership in Ḥijāz, and qaṣīda poetry, especially a poem distinct from rajaz.

TABRISI:18:17-18/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:17-18/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:17-18/r2.claim: Tazāwar can derive from tatazāwar with assimilation of tāʾ into zāy, or from deletion of the second tāʾ; Abū al-Ḥasan objects that the form tazūr does not fit here, while Abū ʿAlī adduces Jarīr’s poetic use of azwirār for tents.

TABRISI:18:17-18/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:17-18/r3.speaker: أبو الحسن
TABRISI:18:17-18/r3.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan says tazūr has no suitable sense here and cites azwara ʿannī for withdrawing, as in ʿAntara’s poem about a spear wound.

TABRISI:18:17-18/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:17-18/r4.speaker: جرير
TABRISI:18:17-18/r4.claim: Jarīr’s verse describing tents with azwirār supports the use of a form meaning to turn or slant away.

TABRISI:18:17-18/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:17-18/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:18:17-18/r8.claim: Qarḍ can mean cutting across or passing by; al-Kisāʾī also gives it the sense of reciprocal recompense, as in Dhū al-Rumma’s line about traversing a valley.

TABRISI:18:17-18/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:18:17-18/r9.speaker: أبو الدرداء
TABRISI:18:17-18/r9.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ uses qāraḍtuhum for trading insults: if you criticize them, they will criticize you.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r1.claim: They read تزاور with a doubled zāy.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r10.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r10.claim: They say the cave faced the Pleiades in Roman territory, so the sun avoided entering and harming the sleepers with heat or changing their color.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r11.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r11.claim: فجوة means an open, spacious place; its plural forms include فجوات and فجاء.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r12.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r12.claim: The sun's deflection is a divine sign; he rejects the claim that the cave faced the Pleiades.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r13.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r13.claim: The spacious cave let cool breezes reach them; its protection from sun, along with the fear cast over others, displays God's power and care.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r14.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r14.claim: The statement that God guides whoever He wills explains that He personally guided the youths; without that guidance they would not have found the way.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r2.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r2.claim: They read تزاور with a light, undoubled zāy.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r4.speaker: أبي بن كعب وأبو مجلز وأبو رجاء والجحدري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r4.claim: They read تزوار, with a still zāy and a lengthened alif after wāw.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r5.speaker: ابن مسعدو وأبو المتوكل وابن السميفع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r5.claim: They read تزوئر with hamza before rāʾ, like تزوعر.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r6.speaker: أبو الجوزاء وأبو السماك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r6.claim: They read تزور with fatḥa on tāʾ and zāy and a doubled, open wāw.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r7.claim: The root form is تتزاور, with tāʾ assimilated into zāy; the word means to incline and turn aside.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r8.claim: تقرضهم means the sun turns away from and leaves them; the root قرض conveys cutting and separation, as in lending someone a dirham from one's own money.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r9.speaker: ذو الرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p117/r9.claim: His cited line uses يقرضن to mean that the camels leave something behind.

RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r10.claim: The doubled form comes from tat-zāwar with assimilation, the light form is a reciprocal form from zawr, and tazawwar derives from izwirār.

RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r11.claim: “You see the sun” addresses a hypothetical observer; it means that were the addressee to see it, the sun would incline from the cave.

RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r12.claim: Dhāt al-yamīn means the right-hand direction; dhāt, the feminine of dhū, stands in place of the noun it qualifies.

RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r8.speaker: ابن عامر
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads tazawwar with a still zāy and doubled rāʾ, like taḥmar.

RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r9.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v21p84#2/r9.claim: ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read tazāwar with an alif and lightening; the remaining readers double it. The readings all mean to incline.

RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r1.speaker: الكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r1.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says qaraḍtu al-makān means to turn aside from a place.

RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda gives qarḍ several senses including cutting across, so the sun passes away from their heads toward the north.

RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r3.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r3.claim: One interpretation says the cave opening faced north, keeping direct sunlight out while pleasant air entered and prevented decay or damage to the youths' bodies.

RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r4.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj argues that God miraculously prevented sunlight from reaching them: the ordinary north-facing-cave account would not itself be a sign.

RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r5.claim: They lay in a spacious part of the cave where air and cool breezes could reach them; fajwa means an open, roomy space.

RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r6.claim: Abū ʿUbayda gives fajawāt as the plural of fajwa and cites a report about moving briskly when finding open space.

RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r7.claim: For those accepting divine prevention of sunlight, “that” refers to the sun's deviation; for others it means God's long protection of them in the cave.

RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p85/r8.claim: Their turn from unbelief to faith, like their bodily preservation, came by God's aid; the guided youths contrast with Daqyānūs and his unbelieving followers, and the verse raises known debates on predestination.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r1.claim: The sun turns away from the cave at sunrise; the address is hypothetical, meaning that a viewer would see this, not that the Prophet actually saw them.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r10.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r10.claim: The majority reading has the sun leave them at sunset; Mujahid glosses taqriḍuhum as 'leave them.'

QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r11.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r11.claim: Qatada glosses the verb as 'abandon them'; Basran authorities confirm that qarada can mean leave.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas says the sun never touched them, as an honor: it passed to the cave's right at sunrise and left by its left at sunset.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r13.claim: The cave faced Banat Naʿsh in Roman territory; its orientation or southern and western barriers kept sun from burning them, changing their color, or wearing their clothes.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r14.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r14.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the sun's course was a divine sign, not an effect of the cave opening's orientation.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r15.speaker: فرقة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r15.claim: A group reads the verb with yāʾ from qard, meaning the cave's shade cuts them off from sunlight.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r16.speaker: فرقة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r16.claim: Another interpretation says the sun gives them only a little of its rays, perhaps beneficial in the evening.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r17.claim: The point is that God sheltered them in a cave that protected their bodies and appearance from injury, heat, and cold; cloud or another cause could have diverted the sun.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r18.claim: Fajwa means a spacious part of the cave; the word has plural forms and denotes enough room for moving air to reach them.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r19.speaker: شاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r19.claim: The author introduces a poetic example after listing the plural forms of fajwa.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r2.claim: Tazawaru means to withdraw or incline, from azwar, a slant; azwar can describe a gaze turned aside and is extended beyond eyes.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r3.speaker: ابن أبي ربيعة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r3.claim: Ibn Abi Rabiʿa's line uses azwar for a person turning aside in fear of others.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r4.speaker: عنترة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r4.claim: Antara's line uses azwara for turning aside from the impact of a spear.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r5.claim: The Mu'ta report describes Abd Allah ibn Rawaha's bier as slanted away from the biers of Jaʿfar and Zayd.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r6.speaker: أهل الحرمين وأبو عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r6.claim: They assimilate the tāʾ into zāy in tazāwaru, whose underlying form is tatazāwaru.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r7.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r7.claim: They read tazāwaru with a light zāy.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r8.speaker: ابن عامر
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r8.claim: Ibn Amir reads tazawwaru, like taḥmaru.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r9.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:18:17-18/r9.claim: Al-Farraʾ also records tazwāru, like taḥmāru; all these forms mean the same thing.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:17-18/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:17-18/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:17-18/r1.claim: The sun's rays miss the youths because the cave faces south, or because God diverted the sun; the forms تزاور, تزور, and تزوار all mean to incline.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:17-18/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:17-18/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:17-18/r2.claim: The Kufans drop the initial tā; Ibn Amir and Yaqub read تزور, and another reading is تزوار.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:17-18/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:17-18/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:17-18/r3.claim: At sunset the light cuts past the cave's sides; the youths lie in its broad middle, where air reaches without narrow-cave stuffiness or damaging solar heat.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:17-18/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:17-18/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:17-18/r4.claim: The cave's entrance faces the stars of the Great Bear; the sun's seasonal paths illuminate its sides to ventilate and purify it without harming the sleepers or their clothes.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:17-18/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:17-18/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:17-18/r5.claim: The sign may be the sleepers and their cave, the revealed story, or the sun's turning away and grazing past them; guidance benefits only those enabled to reflect.

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:17-18/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:17-18/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:17-18/r6.claim: One who is left astray will find no protector to guide him.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p6#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6#2/r1.claim: Readings include tazāwar, tazūr, and tazāwar; the first is from tatāzāwar, reduced by assimilation or deletion, and the root denotes turning aside.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p6#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6#2/r2.claim: At sunrise the sun inclines away from the cave so its rays do not fall on the sleepers; at sunset it leaves them on the other side.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p6#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6#2/r3.claim: Taqriḍuhum means that the sun cuts past them, leaves them, and turns away; they remain shaded through the day despite the cave's openness.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p6#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6#2/r4.claim: One explanation says the cave's spacious opening let them receive fresh air and cool breezes without suffering the cave's confinement.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p6#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6#2/r5.claim: The sun's unusual avoidance of them, though it ordinarily reaches that exposed place, is a divine sign and a special honor for them.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p6#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6#2/r6.claim: Another explanation makes the cave's north-facing entrance keep the sleepers perpetually in shade; their story itself is also called a sign.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p6#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p6#2/r7.claim: Their guidance is praise for striving in God and submitting to Him, through which He led them to this noble honor; one whom God misleads has no guide.

QASHANI:18:17/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:17/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:17/r1.claim: The sun is spirit: rising through detachment from the body turns them toward holiness and good works; setting into the body veils them and turns them toward the soul, sins, and evil.

QASHANI:18:17/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:17/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:17/r2.claim: The open space is soul and nature in the body beyond spirit's light; the heart's spirit-facing side is illuminated intellect and angelic inspiration, while its soul-facing side is dark chest and satanic whispering.

QASHANI:18:17/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:17/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:17/r3.claim: Turning toward spirit illuminates the heart and draws it to good; turning toward soul obscures it and draws it to sin, while angelic inspiration and satanic whisper can mingle in deeds.

QASHANI:18:17/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:17/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:17/r4.claim: The text turns them away from the cave when they incline to good but cuts them off when they incline to evil, showing a traveler still in changing states rather than settled station.

QASHANI:18:17/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:17/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:17/r5.claim: The spirit's rising and hiding are signs for guidance: one whom God brings to witnessing and settledness is truly guided, while the veiled have no guide; alternatively, some are guided to know their state and others screened from it.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r10.speaker: عنترة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r10.claim: ʿAntara’s line uses azwar for turning aside from a spear’s impact.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r11.speaker: بشر بن أبي حازم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r11.claim: Bishr ibn Abī Ḥāzim’s verse witnesses the noun azwirār for a directional deviation.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r12.claim: Qaraḍa means cut off; Kufans instead say it can mean to approach or move alongside a place, citing Bedouin usage.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r13.speaker: الكوفيون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r13.claim: The Kufans report Arabs saying qaraḍtahu qablan wa-dabran for approaching something from its front and back.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r14.claim: Fajwa is an open space, from a root describing separation between the thighs; fajāʾ is its plural.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r8.claim: Tazāwar means turn away or incline; al-Akhfash glosses it as withdrawing, and azwar can describe an eye or anything that leans.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r9.speaker: ابن أبي ربيعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p132/r9.claim: Ibn Abī Rabīʿa’s verse witnesses the use of azwar for one who leans or turns aside.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r10.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق وطلحة والأعمش وباقي السبعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r10.claim: These readers use تزور, on the pattern of تحمر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r11.speaker: الجحدري وأبو رجاء وأيوب السختياني وابن أبي عبلة وجابر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r11.claim: These readers use تزوار, on the pattern of تحمار; this reading is also reported from Ayyūb.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r7.claim: The account omits connecting events: the youths entered the cave, God caused sleep, answered their prayer, and provided comforts there.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r8.speaker: الحرميان وأبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r8.claim: The Ḥaramayn readers and Abū ʿAmr assimilate the tāʾ of تتزاور into zāy.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r9.speaker: الكوفيون والأعمش وطلحة وابن أبي ليلى وابن مناذر وخلف وأبو عبيد وابن سعدان ومحمد بن عيسى الأصبهاني وأحمد بن جبير الأنطاكي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p150#2/r9.claim: This group reads the verb with a light zāy after deleting the tāʾ.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو المتوكل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Abū al-Mutawakkil read تزوئر with hamza before rāʾ, as in other hamzated forms to avoid two adjacent sukūns; it means turn or incline away.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r10.speaker: أبو علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r10.claim: Abū ʿAlī reads تقرضهم as giving them some sunlight briefly, like a loan that is taken back; he says the sun touched them lightly morning and evening.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r11.claim: He rejects the loan derivation: that would require a different four-letter verb and vowel pattern; تقرضهم instead means cuts off some of its light for them.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r12.claim: God placed them where sun was limited enough to avoid heat but not wholly absent, preventing stale air and decay; this special solar path is a sign of divine care.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r13.claim: If the cave faced Banāt Naʿsh and naturally blocked the sun, the signs include their monotheistic guidance, shelter, protection, awe, preserved bodies and clothes, and sleep through the long period.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r2.claim: ذات اليمين means the cave’s right-hand side, defined from the entrant’s or youths’ perspective; تقرضهم means cuts them off rather than approaching them.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r3.claim: Most readers pronounce تقرضهم with tāʾ; another group reads يقرضهم, making the cave the subject that keeps the sun off them.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the sun did not touch the youths at all.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r5.speaker: فرقة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r5.claim: Another group says afternoon sun reached them in a way beneficial to their bodies; this implies barriers to south and west and a corner position.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن مسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r6.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. Muslim says the cave entrance faced the Banāt Naʿsh stars, which would leave its upper part sheltered from rain.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the cave faced Banāt Naʿsh, so neither sunrise nor sunset entered; God chose a broad, airy shaded resting place that avoided the cave’s distress.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says they stayed in shade all day despite an open, broad site exposed to the sun, which God screened from them.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r9.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p151/r9.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the sun’s behavior itself is a sign; the cave need not face a direction that naturally causes it.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p152/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p152/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p152/r1.claim: The guidance statement is general: it includes the cave youths as those guided and Daqyānūs and his followers as those led astray.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p152/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p152/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p152/r2.claim: The address in وترى الشمس and وتحسبهم is to anyone who might see the cave.

SAMIN-DURR:18:17#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:17#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:17#2/r1.claim: The alternative parse makes ذلك the predicate of omitted الأمر and من آيات الله a circumstantial phrase.

SAMIN-DURR:18:17#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:17#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:17#2/r2.claim: ذات اليمين and ذات الشمال are spatial adverbials meaning the two directions.

SAMIN-DURR:18:17#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:17#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:17#2/r3.claim: وهم في فجوة منه is circumstantial; the sun's avoidance despite open space makes their protection more striking; فجوة means open space.

SAMIN-DURR:18:17#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:17#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:17#2/r4.claim: ذلك refers to their whole story as subject of من آيات الله, or is a predicate of omitted الأمر with من آيات الله circumstantial.

SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r1.claim: Ibn Amir reads تزور, meaning it inclines; زور is deviation and الأزور describes a slanting eye or body.

SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r10.speaker: الفارسي
SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r10.claim: Al-Farisi instead says the sun lends them light and quickly withdraws it; the author says that sense should use passive تُقرضهم.

SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r11.claim: A ياء reading gives the cave as subject, but Ibn Kaysan prefers keeping the sun as subject in both clauses.

SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r2.speaker: عمر بن أبي ربيعة
SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r2.claim: Umar ibn Abi Rabi'a's line uses أزور for a slanting posture.

SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r3.claim: Another gloss is recoil or contraction, from ازور; Antara's فازور from spear impact supports this sense.

SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r4.speaker: بشر بن أبي خازم
SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r4.claim: Bishr ibn Abi Khazim uses ازورار for inclination.

SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r5.claim: Kufis lighten ز in تزاور; others double it. Both derive from تتزاور by dropping one ت or assimilation.

SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r6.claim: Abu Raja and others read تزوار; Abdullah and Abu al-Mutawakkil read تزوئر, replacing alif in تزوار with hamza to avoid adjacent sukun.

SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r7.claim: إذا طلعت may attach to ترى or تزاور; إذا غربت to ترى or تقرضهم; they are mainly temporal but may be conditional.

SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r8.claim: تقرضهم means the sun cuts them off; قرض means cutting or separation, supported by Dhu al-Rumma's line.

SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:17/r9.claim: Dhu al-Rumma uses يقرضن for cutting across mountain ridges.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p142/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p142/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p142/r1.claim: The cave entrance faced north: sunrise falls away to the right as the shadow recedes, then sunlight passes them to the left at sunset; Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Qatada gloss tazawwar as inclining.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p142/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p142/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p142/r2.claim: The sun's path rules out an eastern entrance, which would receive no sunset rays; a southern entrance, which would receive neither sunrise nor sunset rays; and a western entrance, which would get no light until after noon.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p142/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p142/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p142/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and others explain taqriduhum as passing them by or leaving them; Malik from Zayd ibn Aslam glosses tazawwar as inclining.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p142/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p142/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p142/r4.claim: The cave's location has no religious benefit; proposed sites include near Aila according to Ibn Abbas, near Nineveh according to Ibn Ishaq, and Roman or Balqa lands, but scripture and the Prophet's teaching give no reason to identify it.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p142/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p142/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p142/r5.claim: The youths lay in a roomy interior space where sunlight did not touch them, since direct exposure would burn their bodies and clothes.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p143/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p143/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p143/r1.claim: The cave was a sign because God guided the youths to shelter where they remained alive and sunlight and wind could reach them to preserve their bodies.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p143/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p143/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p143/r2.claim: God alone guided the youths; whoever He guides is rightly guided, while a person He misleads has no guide or protecting ally.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p451#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451#2/r1.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451#2/r1.claim: These readers assimilate the ta of the tafaʿul form in تزاور.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p451#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451#2/r2.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451#2/r2.claim: These readers omit the ta in the recitation of تزاور.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p451#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451#2/r3.speaker: ابن عامر ويعقوب
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451#2/r3.claim: They read تزور on the pattern of تحمر, which the author relates to the sun's state at the end of its inclination.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p451#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451#2/r4.claim: The sun inclines away at dawn and veers aside at sunset so its warmth benefits the sleepers without overheating or harming them.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p451#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451#2/r5.claim: The author infers a cave entrance facing Banat Naash and a mountain north of Mecca, but says the directions may instead be relative to someone leaving the cave.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p451#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451#2/r6.speaker: الأصبهاني
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451#2/r6.claim: Al-Asbahani reports that the cave entrance faced north, with sunrise to its right and sunset to its left.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p451#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p451#2/r7.claim: The root of قرض centers on cutting, from which the senses of veering aside, passing, and giving a loan cut from one's wealth are derived.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p452/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p452/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p452/r1.claim: The sleepers lie in the cave's broad central space, where fresh air helps preserve them from decay and other harm.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p452/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p452/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p452/r2.claim: Their guidance, planning, and the cave's protective ventilation are signs of God's knowledge and power, even if small beside the Qur'an.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p452/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p452/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p452/r3.claim: Only those whom God guides benefit from His signs; the misguided see and hear them but fail to understand or use them.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p452/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p452/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p452/r4.claim: The passage uses احتباك: guidance in the first clause implies omitted misguidance, while the later mention of a guiding protector implies an omitted misleader.

DURR-FULL:v5p365/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p365/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p365/r5.claim: The cave's sunlight would have burned the sleepers, and without God turning them from side to side the earth would have consumed them.

DURR-FULL:v5p371/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p371/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p371/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says تزاور means to incline and تقرضهم means to leave them.

DURR-FULL:v5p371/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p371/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p371/r4.claim: Mujahid likewise glosses تقرضهم as leaving them and فجوة as the inner part of a place.

DURR-FULL:v5p371/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p371/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p371/r5.claim: The فجوة is an open, unoccupied area of land, a corner or side of the earth.

DURR-FULL:v5p371/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p371/r6.speaker: أبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v5p371/r6.claim: Abu Malik explains فجوة as a side or corner.

BURSEVI:v5p173#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p173#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p173#2/r1.claim: At sunset the sun cuts past without approaching them; al-Qāmūs glosses this as passing by and leaving them on its left, the eastern side of the cave.

BURSEVI:v5p173#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p173#2/r2.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v5p173#2/r2.claim: The lexicon glosses the sun passing them on the left as leaving them to the north, passing by, cutting past, and leaving them on its left.

BURSEVI:v5p173#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p173#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p173#2/r3.claim: Fajwah means open space or broad courtyard; the circumstantial clause stresses the marvel that the sun avoids them all day although their spacious position is exposed to it.

BURSEVI:v5p173#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p173#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p173#2/r4.claim: The sun's course is a wondrous sign of God's knowledge and power, the truth of monotheism, and His honoring those devoted to Him.

BURSEVI:v5p173#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p173#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p173#2/r5.claim: The guidance statement either praises the youths as guided or teaches that signs benefit only those God enables to discern them; whoever chooses misguidance has no possible protecting guide.

BURSEVI:v5p173/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p173/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p173/r1.claim: The address in ترى may be to Muhammad or anyone capable of seeing; it describes what one would see at the cave, not an event actually witnessed.

BURSEVI:v5p173/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p173/r2.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p173/r2.claim: His story says a shepherd led the youths into the cave, God caused them to sleep, Decianus later learned of their flight and sealed the entrance to kill them inside, while two believing courtiers recorded their names and story on a stone tablet for a future discoverer.

BURSEVI:v5p173/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p173/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p173/r3.claim: The sun's turning and passing describes the time before Decianus sealed the cave, since sunlight could not enter a sealed entrance and need to be diverted.

BURSEVI:v5p173/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p173/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p173/r4.claim: Tazāwar means turning and inclining, with one of the two tāʾs omitted; the right side faces west for someone facing the cave's depth, and the south-facing cave or miraculous diversion keeps the sun from them.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r1.claim: The sun's movement describes the youths after they entered the cave, inferred from the earlier mention of their taking refuge and the cave being theirs; other narrative details are also omitted.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r10.speaker: أبو الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r10.claim: Abu al-Hasan claims the verse's verb has no meaning here because azwar means contraction; the author calls this an attack on Ibn Amir's reading that distorts his attribution.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r11.claim: The sun turns away from their cave; idafa to them is by loose association, and dhat al-yamin means the cave's right side when entering or the youths' right, a locative phrase.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r12.speaker: المبرد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r12.claim: Al-Mubarrad says dhat al-yamin and dhat al-shimal are flexible adverbial expressions, like yamina and shimala.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r2.claim: The omission may also signal that their following wise advice was obvious; the address is to the Prophet or any suitable observer and emphasizes visibility rather than an actual sighting.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r3.speaker: الكوفيون
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r3.claim: The Kufan and several other readers pronounce tazāwar with two original tāʾs, deleting one for ease.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r4.speaker: الحرميان وأبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r4.claim: The Harami readers and Abu Amr read tazāwar with an open tāʾ and geminated zāy, assimilating the first tāʾ after it changes to zāy.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r5.speaker: ابن إسحاق وابن عامر وقتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r5.claim: Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Amir, Qatada, Humayd, and others read tazawwar, a rare verb form outside the usual defect and color meanings.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r6.speaker: جابر والجحدري وأبو رجاء
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r6.claim: Jabir, al-Jahdari, Abu Rajaʾ, and others read tazwār, another rare derived form.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r7.claim: Ibn Masud and Abu al-Mutawakkil read tazwāʾr, inserting a hamza to avoid two adjacent still letters.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r8.claim: All these readings derive from zawr, meaning inclination or deviation; its scope is general, though some restrict it to a natural inclination, and poets use the root of bodily leaning.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r9.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v15p221#2/r9.claim: Al-Raghib links zawr to the upper chest and says azwar is one whose chest inclines; visiting someone can mean turning one's chest toward him, though the author favors the common derivation.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r1.speaker: الكسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r1.claim: Al-Kisai says qarada a place means to turn away from it without coming near.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r10.claim: Some instead take qarada as cutting light off for them, supplying an omitted laam; this was motivated by fear that total shade would spoil the air, but most commentators say sunlight never touched them.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r11.claim: A group also prefers God's miraculous shielding, which the demonstrative supports; extraordinary preservation is apt in a story already full of wonders.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r2.claim: Dhat al-shimal is the cave's left side, toward the east; other authorities derive the verb from “cutting” and understand the sun as passing beyond the sleepers.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r3.speaker: ذو الرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r3.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's line witnesses qarada in the sense of cutting through or across a place.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r4.claim: The youths lay in a broad part of the cave; the word faja is also used for space between the thighs and has several plural forms.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسلم وابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r5.claim: One explanation says the cave's orientation made sunlight strike the sides to refresh the air without touching the sleepers: its entrance faced the Pleiades, and the sun's seasonal path passed beside it.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r6.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects the geometry and says God miraculously diverted the sun so it never struck them, as a sign of power and honor for the faithful.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r7.claim: The author favors miraculous shielding: the phrase “that is among God's signs” supports it more clearly and shows divine power, true monotheism, and honor for the faithful.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r8.speaker: أبو علي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r8.claim: Abu Ali reads qarada as lending them some sunlight temporarily and quickly taking it back, so the sun misses them in the morning but lightly touches them in the evening.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p222/r9.claim: The author objects that the triliteral verb qaraḍa with that meaning is unattested, so the proposed morphology has no basis.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p223/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
